correctness.rationale: A JR-eligible bloc has precisely one quota; the number of seats forces one selected party maximum, and stronger EJR has no higher-level cohesive groups. Sum-of-top-k and maxima identities are exact. Tail integration proves the finite expressions; the top-k CVaR variational identity yields an O_p(1) quantile-linearization error, followed by an iid block CLT. Exact uniform expected loss, covariance and ratio CLT were independently rederived and tested in verify_price.py; no finite numerical test is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The question arises naturally when the exact voter quota requires one quality-scored candidate from each equally sized party. Rather than arbitrary parameter slices, the theorem gives the full iid-distribution law at fixed party-list size, exact finite uniform expected welfare price, universal sharp 8/9 ratio in the two-candidate case, and quantitatively calibrated Gaussian coupled fluctuations (variance 1/72 and ratio variance 52/2187). It distinguishes average welfare under classical representation from existing deterministic quality guarantees and can serve as a numerical benchmark. Neither basic JR equivalence nor raw correctness alone is presented as the value.
